summary_en: Memberships, desk booking, billing and community for flexible workspace.
summary_fr: Abonnements, réservation de postes, facturation et animation d'espaces flexibles.

tools.name: Archie
tools.positioning: Space management software for hybrid offices and coworking spaces, priced per desk and room rather than per user.
tools.description: Archie is a workplace and coworking management platform covering desk booking, meeting room booking, and visitor management, sold as separate modules that can be bought together or on their own. It serves both corporate hybrid-office teams and commercial flex-space operators from the same codebase.
tools.real_estate_use: A flex-space operator or corporate workplace team uses Archie to manage floor plans, let members or employees reserve a desk or room from a web or mobile app, check visitors in at reception, and see office occupancy across one or several locations. Multi-location operators use it to keep a consistent booking and billing experience across sites without building their own scheduling logic.
features: Desk booking with visual floor plans
Meeting room booking with calendar sync
Visitor management and check-in
Membership and recurring billing
Occupancy analytics
SSO and SCIM for larger accounts

use_cases.job: Run desk and room booking across a single or multi-location flex space from one admin console
Track office occupancy and manage visitor check-in for a hybrid workplace

tools.name: Cobot
tools.positioning: Straightforward coworking management for a single space that does not want an enterprise platform.
tools.description: Cobot handles coworking administration: member sign-up and plans, invoicing and payments, meeting room bookings, a member directory, check-in and access integrations, and reporting, aimed at independent spaces rather than multi-site operators.
tools.real_estate_use: An independent space with sixty members needs billing that runs itself and a booking calendar members can trust, not revenue management. Cobot's appeal is that it can be set up in a day by the person who also makes the coffee, and its open API keeps custom door-access and signage projects possible.
features: Member plans, sign-up flows and automated invoicing
Meeting room booking with member allowances
Payment processing and dunning
Member directory and community profiles
Access control and check-in integrations
Open API and webhooks

use_cases.job: Run billing and bookings for an independent coworking space single-handed
Convert spare floor space into a small membership operation

tools.name: Cosoft
tools.positioning: All-in-one management platform for coworking spaces, tiers-lieux and fablabs, covering booking, billing, door access and community.
tools.description: Cosoft is a French SaaS platform for running shared workspaces, published by FTEL. It handles desk and meeting-room booking on an interactive calendar, online payment, automatic quotes and invoices with an accounting export, a member community layer, and connections to door-access, wifi and printing systems. It is sold as a free tier, a Premium plan at a published monthly price and a quoted Pro plan that adds multi-site management, a prospecting CRM and API access. The editor counts forty connected partners, fifteen of them online payment providers and seventeen access-control systems.
tools.real_estate_use: A coworking or tiers-lieu manager uses Cosoft as the operating system of the site: members book a desk or a meeting room themselves and pay online, the invoice and the accounting export follow without re-keying, and the door opens on a badge or from a phone. Local authorities running a tiers-lieu reach for it for the same reasons plus the occupancy figures they have to report. The community side, directory and posts and chat and paid or free events, is what a manager uses to keep the place alive once the operational part runs itself. Multi-site and the API sit in the top plan, which is where a small network of spaces lands rather than a single site.
features: Interactive booking calendar for desks, private offices and meeting rooms
Automatic quote and invoice generation with ready-made accounting export
Online payment through fifteen connected payment providers
Door access managed through seventeen connected access-control systems
Member community layer: directory, posts, chat, email campaigns, events
Prospecting CRM and API access on the top plan

use_cases.job: Run booking, billing and door access for a shared workspace without re-keying anything between tools
Track occupancy and revenue across several shared workspaces from one dashboard

tools.name: CoworkSaaS
tools.positioning: Coworking management software built around its own access control, so a space can stay open around the clock and bill by the hour.
tools.description: CoworkSaaS is a French platform for coworking operators that couples subscription and hourly-access management with an access-control system of its own: QR-code readers, turnstiles and door-locking kits rented monthly alongside the software. Members sign up from the operator's own website, receive a personal QR code, and are billed either on a recurring plan or on the time actually spent on site, computed from entry and exit scans. Additional services are billed through the same engine: meeting rooms, printing, lockers, business domiciliation, a connected fridge. A pooled remote video-surveillance service is offered for unstaffed hours. Two plans are published, per space per month.
tools.real_estate_use: The problem this addresses is opening hours. An operator who wants to sell access outside staffed hours has to know who is in the building and to bill them with nobody at the desk; CoworkSaaS answers both with one QR code, since the scan that opens the turnstile also starts the meter. Hourly billing is the part most competitors do not cover, and it is what lets a space sell to occasional users who would never take a monthly plan. Sign-up and the client area are embedded in the operator's own website, so a prospect never leaves the brand, and a live counter of free seats can be published to members.
features: Hourly access billed from entry and exit QR-code scans
Proprietary access control: QR readers, turnstiles and door-locking kits
Recurring subscription billing with automatic payment
Sign-up and client-area modules embedded in the operator's own website
Additional services engine: meeting rooms, printing, lockers, domiciliation
Pooled remote video surveillance for unstaffed hours

use_cases.job: Keep a coworking space open around the clock and know at any minute who is inside
Sell hourly access to occasional users and bill it automatically on time spent

tools.name: DollyDesk
tools.positioning: Flat-price booking and billing software for a single coworking space of up to fifty desks, with an interactive floor plan.
tools.description: DollyDesk is a French coworking management tool sold at one flat price rather than per member, for up to fifty bookable desks and meeting rooms. Members choose a seat on an interactive floor plan that shows photos of each space, then pay by card through Stripe or through PayFiP for publicly run spaces, or by recurring SEPA direct debit. It issues electronic invoices through an approved platform, exports to accounting, syncs bookings to Google, Outlook and Apple calendars over iCal, and opens Nuki or SmartAir smart locks as a paid option. Prepaid packs, for instance ten days, are supported alongside contracts. The product is operated and supported by a single person, who also handles migration from Nexudus, OfficeRnD or Cosoft.
tools.real_estate_use: A small coworking space or tiers-lieu reaches for DollyDesk when the manager's day is eaten by two questions, is there a seat free and where is my invoice. Members answer both themselves: they see the plan, book, pay, and get the invoice. Because PayFiP is supported next to Stripe, a space run by a local authority can take payments the way public accounting requires, which most competitors do not cover. The flat price and the fifty-desk ceiling say plainly who this is for: one site with a handful of rooms, not a network, and an operator who would rather pay a fixed line than a per-member one.
features: Interactive floor plan with photos for choosing a desk or a room
Flat single price up to fifty desks, not billed per member
Card payment through Stripe or PayFiP, plus recurring SEPA direct debit
Automated electronic invoicing through an approved platform
Prepaid booking packs, for example a ten-day pass
iCal sync to Google, Outlook and Apple calendars, with optional e-ink room displays

use_cases.job: Let members book and pay for a desk on their own, evenings and weekends included
Run a publicly funded tiers-lieu where payments must go through PayFiP

tools.name: essensys
tools.positioning: The infrastructure layer under flex space — network, access and billing for buildings running many operators.
tools.description: essensys provides software and on-site technology for flexible workspace: operations and billing platform, plus network infrastructure that segments and provisions connectivity per tenant, and access control across multi-tenant buildings.
tools.real_estate_use: A landlord converting floors to flex has a problem no coworking app solves: every occupier needs its own secure network segment, provisioned in hours rather than weeks, and metered. essensys sits at that layer, which is why it is bought by landlords and large operators rather than by single spaces.
features: Per-tenant network provisioning and segmentation
Automated billing for space, services and consumption
Access control across multi-tenant buildings
Operations platform for flexible workspace portfolios
Real-time service usage metering
Landlord-grade reporting across operators

use_cases.job: Turn floors into flex space with secure per-occupier networks provisioned in hours
Meter and bill services consumed by multiple operators in one building

tools.name: Nexudus
tools.positioning: The configurable veteran of coworking software — if your operating model is unusual, this is the one that bends.
tools.description: Nexudus covers coworking and flexible workspace management: bookings, billing, CRM, a white-label member portal and app, community features, access and printing integrations, and a large set of configuration options and add-ons.
tools.real_estate_use: Flex operators rarely run the same model twice — credit systems for room hours, tiered plans, franchise structures, mixed private-office and hot-desk inventory. Nexudus is chosen for the depth of configuration that supports those variations, and for white labelling when the operator's brand must be the only one members see.
features: Membership, contract and recurring billing configuration
White-label member portal and mobile app
Meeting room booking with credit and allowance systems
Access control, printing and network integrations
CRM, marketing and community tools
Multi-location and franchise structures

use_cases.job: Model an unusual membership and credit structure without leaving the system
Run a fully white-labelled member experience under the operator's own brand

tools.name: OfficeRnD Flex
tools.positioning: The operating system of a coworking business — memberships, bookings, billing and the member app in one product.
tools.description: OfficeRnD Flex manages flexible workspace operations: member and company records, space and desk inventory, contracts and automated recurring billing, meeting room bookings, door access integration, and a member-facing app and portal.
tools.real_estate_use: A flex operator's revenue is a mesh of monthly memberships, day passes, room hours and overage charges — billing that breaks any standard property accounting model. OfficeRnD automates the invoice run and connects it to access control, so a lapsed payment can suspend a badge. Landlords running their own flex floors buy it for the same reason.
features: Membership plans, contracts and automated recurring billing
Desk, office and meeting room inventory and allocation
Member app and portal for bookings and community
Door access control integration tied to membership status
Occupancy, revenue and utilisation analytics
Multi-location management under one operator

use_cases.job: Bill a mesh of memberships, day passes and room hours without manual invoicing
Operate flexible workspace floors inside an owned building

tools.name: Optix
tools.positioning: Automation-first coworking software built to let flex operators scale operations without adding headcount.
tools.description: Optix is a coworking and flex-space management platform (formerly ShareDesk) covering bookings, billing, invoicing, member communications and a white-label member app. Its distinguishing feature is a rules-based automation engine that triggers actions such as billing, notifications or access changes without manual admin work.
tools.real_estate_use: A coworking or flex-space operator uses Optix to run day-to-day operations — desk and room bookings, plan and pass sales, invoicing, visitor management — and to automate recurring admin tasks like billing reminders or check-in notifications through its automation module, so a small on-site team can run more locations without proportionally more staff.
features: Desk and meeting room booking
Rules-based automation engine
Billing, invoicing and plans/passes
White-label member web portal and mobile app
Visitor management
API access and webhooks (Pro plan and above)

use_cases.job: Automate recurring billing and member notifications across one or more coworking locations
Standardize booking, billing and reporting for a multi-location flex portfolio

tools.name: Property Hub
tools.positioning: Salesforce-native CRM built specifically for flexible-workspace operators and the brokers who lease them.
tools.description: Property Hub is a CRM built on the Salesforce platform for operators of flexible workspaces and the commercial real estate brokers who lease them. It manages listings, leads, tours and lease renewals in one place, and adds flex-market analytics such as price-per-desk benchmarks on top of standard CRM records.
tools.real_estate_use: A flex-space operator's leasing team tracks incoming leads and scheduled tours for available desks and suites across its portfolio, and follows upcoming lease renewals from the same pipeline. A CRE broker specializing in flexible offices uses the same platform to match a client's requirement against available flex inventory and to check price-per-desk benchmarks for a given market before making an offer.
features: Flexible-workspace listing and lead management
Tour scheduling
Lease-renewal tracking
Flex-market price benchmarking (price per desk)
Native Salesforce integration with 500+ apps via API

use_cases.job: Track leads, tours and lease renewals for flexible-workspace inventory across a portfolio
Match a client's requirement to available flex-office inventory and check price-per-desk benchmarks

tools.name: Spacebring
tools.positioning: Coworking software built for operators who run their space from a phone rather than a back office.
tools.description: Spacebring is a coworking management platform combining billing, bookings, access and community into a single member web portal and white-label mobile app. It targets independent and small multi-location operators rather than large enterprise flex brands.
tools.real_estate_use: A coworking operator uses Spacebring to sign up new members, run recurring billing automatically, let members book desks and rooms from a branded app, and manage day-to-day operations from a phone rather than a dedicated back-office team — useful for operators running one or a handful of locations with a lean staff.
features: Member web portal and white-label mobile app
Automated recurring billing and invoicing
Desk and meeting room booking
Interactive floor plans (add-on)
Access control integrations
Community and communication tools

use_cases.job: Run billing and bookings for an independent coworking space without a dedicated back-office team

tools.name: Tydeck
tools.positioning: Management software for coworking spaces, flex offices and coliving, from client onboarding to automated invoicing and door access.
tools.description: Tydeck is a French platform for operators of shared workspaces, based in Bordeaux. It centralises members and their contracts, offers self-service booking of desks and meeting rooms through a member portal, shows an interactive floor plan of who sits where, issues invoices automatically with SEPA direct debit and a dunning module, and sends contracts and quotes out for electronic signature. Optional modules add a marketplace where the operator publishes its own offers, a Brevo CRM synchronisation and access control through Welcomr or Salto KS. Plans are published and tiered by number of desks, from thirty to a hundred and eighty, with an initial six-month commitment and no setup fee.
tools.real_estate_use: An operator running one or several flex sites uses Tydeck to stop being the booking desk. A new corporate client is created in a couple of minutes, gets an onboarding invitation and enrols its own team; nomadic members book their days of presence from their portal; the invoice, the SEPA mandate and the reminders run without anyone chasing. The interactive floor plan is what the manager watches to read occupancy, and what the member looks at before choosing a seat. Contracts and quotes are signed electronically inside the same tool, which removes the last paper step from letting a desk, and the pricing by desk count rather than by member is what makes it predictable for a site that fills and empties.
features: Interactive floor plan showing real-time desk and room occupancy
Self-service booking portal for resident members and drop-ins
Automatic invoicing with SEPA direct debit and a dunning module
Client onboarding where the client enrols its own team
Electronic signature of contracts and quotes as an optional module
Operator marketplace for publishing additional offers and services

use_cases.job: Onboard a corporate client and let its team book, pay and enter without manual steps
Read occupancy and revenue of a flex site and chase unpaid invoices automatically
